Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.api

Class EditorServices

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.api.EditorServices
public final class EditorServices extends Object
The language's editor services: the answers a tool needs about a buffer rather than from a program.

This is the API the desktop's Espresso editor is built on, and it is public for exactly that reason — an editor should not have to re-implement Mandela's grammar to offer an outline or a completion list, and a third-party tool that writes its own parser will drift from the language the moment the grammar grows a form. Everything here reads the real Parser and the real StandardLibrary tables, so a name offered is a name the language accepts.

Three contracts make this usable on a keystroke:

  • Nothing throws. A buffer is usually mid-edit, so a parse failure is the normal case, not an exception: the outline and the vocabulary answer from the part of the tree that did build, and an unparsable buffer answers empty rather than an error the editor would have to explain.
  • Nothing runs. Services read syntax and the library's tables. The private engine used for the global and module vocabularies is never asked to evaluate a program, so a completion popup cannot execute a script, cannot touch a file and needs no capability decision.
  • Nothing is invented. Members are offered only where the receiver's type is knowable from the buffer — a used module, an annotated or obviously-constructed binding, this inside a declared class, an enum's own name. Where it is a guess, the answer is empty, because a wrong candidate costs the developer more attention than a missing one.

  • Method Details

    • keywords

      public static List<String> keywords()
      Every keyword and contextual word, in the order the language declares them.

      Both sets are included because an editor colours both and a completion list should offer both; Keywords.RESERVED is the subset a name may not use.

      Returns:
      the words, never empty

    • globals

      public static List<String> globals()
      The names a Mandela program may read without declaring them: the library's globals (println, str, typeOf, …).

      The engine's own view of its global table is a compile-time question — which names may a program mention — and it includes the hooks the compiler installs to make use and import work. A completion list is an authoring question, and __use__ is not something a developer should be offered, so every double-underscore name is dropped: that prefix is the language's marker for a name a script never writes.

      Returns:
      the names, sorted so a tool's list is stable between calls

    • moduleNames

      public static List<String> moduleNames()
      The modules a use std.<name> statement can ask for.
      Returns:
      the module names, in the order the library declares them

    • valueMembers

      public static List<String> valueMembers(String typeName)
      The members one of the language's own value types answers to.

      Returns:

    • moduleMembers

      public static List<String> moduleMembers(String module)
      The names a standard module exports, which is what makes json. and fs. completable.

      The lookup asks the library for the names it would install, never for the module object itself, so a gated module such as std.fs contributes its vocabulary without this call needing a capability grant or touching a file.

      Parameters:
      module - the module as written after std., or with the prefix
      Returns:
      its exported names, empty for a module this host does not have

    • outline

      public static List<EditorServices.Entry> outline(String source)
      The declarations in a buffer, in source order, without descending into bodies.

      Class and type members are included and sit next to their owner, because an editor's outline tree is built from the flat order: a method row follows the class row that declares it.

      Parameters:
      source - the buffer text; null is empty
      Returns:
      the rows, empty when nothing parsed

    • vocabulary

      public static List<String> vocabulary(String source)
      Every name a buffer binds: declared types, functions, methods, fields, constants, and every let / var / loop / parameter binding in any scope.

      This is the vocabulary a completion list offers before the host's own names, and it is deliberately scope-blind: an editor that offered only the innermost scope would stop suggesting a name the moment the caret moved, and a script that reads a name out of order is a bug the language reports, not the editor.

      Parameters:
      source - the buffer text; null is empty
      Returns:
      the names, in first-declaration order, without duplicates

      Returns:

    • complete

      public static List<String> complete(String source, int caret, Collection<String> hostGlobals)
      The same, with the names the embedding host has bound.

      A host passes what it gave its engine (doc, args, a callback) so those complete exactly like the language's own globals; the language cannot see them, which is why the parameter exists.

      Parameters:
      source - the whole buffer
      caret - the 0-based caret offset
      hostGlobals - extra names the host bound, in priority order
      Returns:
      ranked candidates, at most MAX_CANDIDATES
